The dataclass is frozen so once an ``ExpectCallable``\n166\t    returns a result it cannot be mutated by downstream consumers.\n167\t    \"\"\"\n168\t\n169\t    name: str\n170\t    passed: bool\n171\t    message: str = \"\"\n172\t    details: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)\n173\t    duration_sec: float = 0.0\n174\t    failure: Optional[\"ExpectFailure\"] = None\n175\t\n176\t    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n177\t        \"\"\"Return a JSON-serialisable mapping per DM-009.\n178\t\n179\t        Uses ``dataclasses.asdict`` so nested dataclasses (notably\n180\t        ``ExpectFailure`` once T01.16 lands) are recursively unwrapped into\n181\t        plain dicts. ``details`` is shallow-copied to break the shared\n182\t        reference with the dataclass instance — callers that mutate the\n183\t        returned mapping must not affect the immutable source.\n184\t        \"\"\"\n185\t\n186\t        payload = dataclasses.asdict(self)\n187\t        # ``asdict`` already returns a fresh mapping, but ``details`` may\n188\t        # contain nested mutable containers (lists of event payloads, etc.).\n189\t        # We rely on ``asdict``'s recursive copy for that — no extra work\n190\t        # needed here. _LifecycleState) -> tuple[EvalStatus, Optional[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(status, error_class)`` for the captured lifecycle state.\n\n    Encodes the status-mapping rules from ``artifacts/D-0048/spec.md``:\n\n    * Any captured harness exception -> ``ERRORED`` with the exception's\n      fully-qualified classname.\n    * Otherwise, all ``ExpectResult.passed == True`` -> Subject to one\nadditive change once OQ-10 closes and R3-mit (T05.23) lands the\nMCP-flaky retry-once branch.\n\n## TL;DR\n\n`superclaude eval run` produces a **deterministic single-pass run**.\nFailed evals are never retried automatically. To re-run a failure after\ndiagnosis, use the `--eval <id>` subset path documented below.\n\n```text\nEvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT = 0\nEvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG       = \"MCP-flaky\"   # future R3-mit hook\n```\n\n## Why no default retry?\n\nThe harness ships a **bounded retry policy** so the run output is\nreproducible and the FR-RPT1 N'-vs-K invariant (one `evals[]` row per\nexpanded eval id) is never violated by hidden re-executions. The\n[design-spec §13][design-spec-13] enumerates the constraints:\n\n[design-spec-13]: ../../.dev/releases/current/cliEval/design-spec.md\n\n> *Failed evals are NOT retried by default. The harness produces a\n> deterministic single-pass run. The user can re-run with `--eval\n> <failed-ids>` after diagnosing.*\n\nConcretely:\n\n* `EvalRunner.__init__` accepts a `retry_count` keyword argument with a\n  default of `0` (the class constant `DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT`). Any\n  non-zero value raises `ValueError` at construction time so an\n  accidental caller cannot silently re-execute a failed eval and break\n  the orchestrator's per-spec accounting.\n* `run_eval` (the FR-LC1 lifecycle skeleton) has no retry loop. A\n  failing `ExpectResult` produces a `FAIL` outcome; a harness exception\n  produces `ERRORED`. Neither path re-enters the lifecycle.\n* The orchestrator (`RunOrchestrator`, T03.15) collects one\n  `EvalOutcome` per submitted future via\n  `concurrent.futures.as_completed` and writes it through to the\n  Reporter. There is no orchestrator-layer retry either.\n\n## Re-running a failed eval — the `--eval` subset path\n\nAfter a run completes, the Reporter writes `summary.{md,json}` to the\nrun directory. Inspect the table to identify failed eval ids, then\nre-run only those evals:\n\n```bash\n# Full suite run (deterministic single pass)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --parallel 8\n\n# Re-run only the failing ids after diagnosis (any number of --eval)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --eval E03 --eval E07\n\n# Quick smoke (3-4 evals); same flag, different subset\nsuperclaude eval run suites/quick.yaml --eval E01 --eval E02\n```\n\nNotes:\n\n* `--eval` accepts the **expanded** id (post-parameterize) so a\n  parameterized eval like `E07[case=a]` is targetable by its full\n  identifier. An id that does not match any expanded eval exits with\n  code 2 (see `tests/cli/eval/test_eval_id_regex.py` and\n  `src/superclaude/cli/eval/commands.py` — FR-CLI3).\n* Subset runs are independent processes — they allocate a fresh\n  `HomeIsolation` per eval and emit a fresh `summary.{md,json}` under\n  their own run directory. There is no shared state with the originating\n  run.\n* `--keep-home` controls whether failed HOMEs survive the second run\n  the same way it does for the first. Default behaviour preserves\n  failed HOMEs and discards successful ones; the `--keep-home` flag\n  forces preservation for both.\n\n## When *will* retries happen? (OQ-10 / R3-mit / T05.23)\n\nThe roadmap reserves one in-process retry for evals whose failure mode\nmatches **MCP server flakiness** (timeout, unreachable) — never for\nassertion failures, never for harness exceptions. The intended UX is:\n\n1. The manifest tags the eval with the future `MCP-flaky` tag.\n2. On the first observed failure that matches the MCP-flaky taxonomy,\n   the runner re-executes the lifecycle exactly once.\n3. The second result is the recorded outcome; the first attempt is\n   preserved in the per-eval JSONL log under a `retry_attempt`\n   namespace.\n\nThis branch is **deferred** until OQ-10 closes and the exact taxonomy\nis empirically resolved (see\n`.dev/releases/current/cliEval/decisions.md §B`). Until then, the\n`MCP_FLAKY_TAG = \"MCP-flaky\"` constant on `EvalRunner` reserves the\nexact tag string the future implementation will look for; tagging a\nmanifest entry with it today is a no-op.\n\n## Operator-facing invariants\n\n* `EvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT` is the canonical pin. Reading it from\n  a script (e.g. CI safety check) lets a deployment confirm the\n  harness build has retries disabled.\n* `EvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG` is the canonical pin for the future\n  retry-once tag string. Manifest tooling can reference it instead of\n  hard-coding `\"MCP-flaky\"`.\n* Any change to either constant requires an updated design-spec entry\n  and an explicit M3/M5 closure record per the OQ-10 decision row.\n\n## See also\n\n* `src/superclaude/cli/eval/runner.py` — `EvalRunner` class body,\n  `DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT` and `MCP_FLAKY_TAG`.\n* `tests/cli/eval/test_retry_policy.py` — regression suite locking the\n  contract in place.\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/design-spec.md §13` — Bounded retry\n  contract.\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/decisions.md §B` — OQ-10 deferral\n  record (target M3/M5).\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/artifacts/D-0051/spec.md` — Per-task\n  deliverable record for T03.08.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":18,"newStart":1,"newLines":29,"lines":["-# Eval Retry Policy (NFR-REL2)","+# Eval Retry Policy (NFR-REL2 + R3-mit)"," ","-**Status:** Stable as of T03.08 (Phase 3, D-0051). The R3-mit retry-once branch landed in T05.23 (Phase 5,\nD-0101) and is opt-in per manifest entry via the `MCP-flaky` tag.\n\n## TL;DR\n\n`superclaude eval run` produces a **deterministic single-pass run** by\ndefault. Failed evals are never retried automatically. To re-run a\nfailure after diagnosis, use the `--eval <id>` subset path documented\nbelow.\n\nThe R3-mit policy (T05.23) adds a single, opt-in exception: an eval\nwhose manifest entry lists `MCP-flaky` in its `requires:` array is\nretried **exactly once** when the first attempt produces a non-PASS\noutcome that maps to a flaky failure mode (FAIL, ERRORED, TIMEOUT).\nThe final outcome — whether the retry recovered to PASS or the failure\npersisted — carries the `mcp_server_flaky` artifact in\n`outcome.artifacts` so post-mortem tooling can identify retries\nwithout re-parsing the per-eval JSONL log.\n\n```text\nEvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT = 0          # NFR-REL2 default\nEvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG       = \"MCP-flaky\" # R3-mit tag (T05.23)\nRetryOncePolicy.MAX_ATTEMPTS   = 2          # original + 1 retry\n```\n\n## Why no default retry?\n\nThe harness ships a **bounded retry policy** so the run output is\nreproducible and the FR-RPT1 N'-vs-K invariant (one `evals[]` row per\nexpanded eval id) is never violated by hidden re-executions. The\n[design-spec §13][design-spec-13] enumerates the constraints:\n\n[design-spec-13]: ../../.dev/releases/current/cliEval/design-spec.md\n\n> *Failed evals are NOT retried by default. The harness produces a\n> deterministic single-pass run. The user can re-run with `--eval\n> <failed-ids>` after diagnosing.*\n\nConcretely:\n\n* `EvalRunner.__init__` accepts a `retry_count` keyword argument with a\n  default of `0` (the class constant `DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT`). Any\n  non-zero value raises `ValueError` at construction time so an\n  accidental caller cannot silently re-execute a failed eval and break\n  the orchestrator's per-spec accounting.\n* `run_eval` (the FR-LC1 lifecycle skeleton) has no retry loop. A\n  failing `ExpectResult` produces a `FAIL` outcome; a harness exception\n  produces `ERRORED`. Neither path re-enters the lifecycle.\n* The orchestrator (`RunOrchestrator`, T03.15) collects one\n  `EvalOutcome` per submitted future via\n  `concurrent.futures.as_completed` and writes it through to the\n  Reporter. There is no orchestrator-layer retry either.\n\n## Re-running a failed eval — the `--eval` subset path\n\nAfter a run completes, the Reporter writes `summary.{md,json}` to the\nrun directory. Inspect the table to identify failed eval ids, then\nre-run only those evals:\n\n```bash\n# Full suite run (deterministic single pass)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --parallel 8\n\n# Re-run only the failing ids after diagnosis (any number of --eval)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --eval E03 --eval E07\n\n# Quick smoke (3-4 evals); same flag, different subset\nsuperclaude eval run suites/quick.yaml --eval E01 --eval E02\n```\n\nNotes:\n\n* `--eval` accepts the **expanded** id (post-parameterize) so a\n  parameterized eval like `E07[case=a]` is targetable by its full\n  identifier. An id that does not match any expanded eval exits with\n  code 2 (see `tests/cli/eval/test_eval_id_regex.py` and\n  `src/superclaude/cli/eval/commands.py` — FR-CLI3).\n* Subset runs are independent processes — they allocate a fresh\n  `HomeIsolation` per eval and emit a fresh `summary.{md,json}` under\n  their own run directory. There is no shared state with the originating\n  run.\n* `--keep-home` controls whether failed HOMEs survive the second run\n  the same way it does for the first. Default behaviour preserves\n  failed HOMEs and discards successful ones; the `--keep-home` flag\n  forces preservation for both.\n\n## When *will* retries happen? Failed evals are never retried automatically. To re-run a\nfailure after diagnosis, use the `--eval <id>` subset path documented\nbelow.\n\nThe R3-mit policy (T05.23) adds a single, opt-in exception: an eval\nwhose manifest entry lists `MCP-flaky` in its `requires:` array is\nretried **exactly once** when the first attempt produces a non-PASS\noutcome that maps to a flaky failure mode (FAIL, ERRORED, TIMEOUT).\nThe final outcome — whether the retry recovered to PASS or the failure\npersisted — carries the `mcp_server_flaky` artifact in\n`outcome.artifacts` so post-mortem tooling can identify retries\nwithout re-parsing the per-eval JSONL log.\n\n```text\nEvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT = 0          # NFR-REL2 default\nEvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG       = \"MCP-flaky\" # R3-mit tag (T05.23)\nRetryOncePolicy.MAX_ATTEMPTS   = 2          # original + 1 retry\n```\n\n## Why no default retry?\n\nThe harness ships a **bounded retry policy** so the run output is\nreproducible and the FR-RPT1 N'-vs-K invariant (one `evals[]` row per\nexpanded eval id) is never violated by hidden re-executions. The\n[design-spec §13][design-spec-13] enumerates the constraints:\n\n[design-spec-13]: ../../.dev/releases/current/cliEval/design-spec.md\n\n> *Failed evals are NOT retried by default. The harness produces a\n> deterministic single-pass run. The user can re-run with `--eval\n> <failed-ids>` after diagnosing.*\n\nConcretely:\n\n* `EvalRunner.__init__` accepts a `retry_count` keyword argument with a\n  default of `0` (the class constant `DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT`). Any\n  non-zero value raises `ValueError` at construction time so an\n  accidental caller cannot silently re-execute a failed eval and break\n  the orchestrator's per-spec accounting.\n* `run_eval` (the FR-LC1 lifecycle skeleton) has no retry loop. A\n  failing `ExpectResult` produces a `FAIL` outcome; a harness exception\n  produces `ERRORED`. Neither path re-enters the lifecycle.\n* The orchestrator (`RunOrchestrator`, T03.15) collects one\n  `EvalOutcome` per submitted future via\n  `concurrent.futures.as_completed` and writes it through to the\n  Reporter. There is no orchestrator-layer retry either.\n\n## Re-running a failed eval — the `--eval` subset path\n\nAfter a run completes, the Reporter writes `summary.{md,json}` to the\nrun directory. Inspect the table to identify failed eval ids, then\nre-run only those evals:\n\n```bash\n# Full suite run (deterministic single pass)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --parallel 8\n\n# Re-run only the failing ids after diagnosis (any number of --eval)\nsuperclaude eval run suites/full.yaml --eval E03 --eval E07\n\n# Quick smoke (3-4 evals); same flag, different subset\nsuperclaude eval run suites/quick.yaml --eval E01 --eval E02\n```\n\nNotes:\n\n* `--eval` accepts the **expanded** id (post-parameterize) so a\n  parameterized eval like `E07[case=a]` is targetable by its full\n  identifier. An id that does not match any expanded eval exits with\n  code 2 (see `tests/cli/eval/test_eval_id_regex.py` and\n  `src/superclaude/cli/eval/commands.py` — FR-CLI3).\n* Subset runs are independent processes — they allocate a fresh\n  `HomeIsolation` per eval and emit a fresh `summary.{md,json}` under\n  their own run directory. There is no shared state with the originating\n  run.\n* `--keep-home` controls whether failed HOMEs survive the second run\n  the same way it does for the first. Default behaviour preserves\n  failed HOMEs and discards successful ones; the `--keep-home` flag\n  forces preservation for both.\n\n## R3-mit retry-once (T05.23 / D-0101)\n\nR3-mit reserves exactly one in-process retry for evals whose failure\nmode matches **MCP server flakiness**. The policy is opt-in per\nmanifest entry and orthogonal to `retry_count`:\n\n1. The manifest tags the eval by including `MCP-flaky` in its\n   `requires:` array (the same field that already carries capability\n   names — no schema migration required).\n2. On the first observed failure whose status is `FAIL`, `ERRORED`,\n   or `TIMEOUT`, the runner re-executes the lifecycle exactly once.\n3. Both the recovered-PASS and persistent-failure paths attach the\n   `mcp_server_flaky` artifact to `outcome.artifacts`. The artifact\n   key's value is the literal string `\"true\"` — the Reporter renders\n   the presence of the key, not its content.\n\n### Taxonomy\n\nThe retry is gated on a fixed status set:\n\n| Status | Eligible for retry? | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| FAIL | Yes | Could be expect-side MCP timeout |\n| ERRORED | Yes | Harness exception (often MCP transport) |\n| TIMEOUT | Yes | Most common MCP-flake signature |\n| PASS | No | Nothing to retry |\n| SKIPPED | No | Capability gate — did not run |\n| INTERRUPTED | No | SIGINT — operator intent |\n| XFAIL / XPASS | No | Expected-failure contract |\n\n### Manifest example\n\n```yaml\nevals:\n  - id: E07\n    title: \"Tavily MCP search returns at least one result\"\n    requires:\n      - mcp.tavily       # capability gate\n      - MCP-flaky        # opt-in to R3-mit retry-once\n    expects: [...]\n```\n\n### Orthogonality with NFR-REL2\n\nThe R3-mit policy is wired through an additive `retry_policy` kwarg on\n`EvalRunner`. It does **not** relax the existing `retry_count != 0`\nconstruction guard — accidental sweeps that hand the runner a non-zero\nretry count still raise `ValueError`. The two mechanisms answer\ndifferent questions:\n\n* `retry_count` (NFR-REL2): \"the operator-facing retry budget\" —\n  pinned to 0 because FR-RPT1 requires one `evals[]` row per expanded\n  eval id.\n* `retry_policy` (R3-mit): \"the per-eval flaky-server escape hatch\" —\n  pinned to a single attempt and only fires on the `MCP-flaky` tag.\n\n### OQ-10 decision\n\nOQ-10 closed in favor of keeping R3-mit at P1: the policy lands\nbehind an opt-in tag rather than being promoted to a default-on\nbehaviour. The taxonomy (`FAIL` / `ERRORED` / `TIMEOUT`) was resolved\nempirically against the M5 test surface; see\n`.dev/releases/current/cliEval/decisions.md §B` and\n`.dev/releases/current/cliEval/artifacts/D-0101/notes.md`.\n\n## Operator-facing invariants\n\n* `EvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT` is the canonical pin. Reading it from\n  a script (e.g. CI safety check) lets a deployment confirm the\n  harness build has retries disabled.\n* `EvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG` is the canonical pin for the future\n  retry-once tag string. Manifest tooling can reference it instead of\n  hard-coding `\"MCP-flaky\"`.\n* Any change to either constant requires an updated design-spec entry\n  and an explicit M3/M5 closure record per the OQ-10 decision row.\n\n## See also\n\n* `src/superclaude/cli/eval/runner.py` — `EvalRunner` class body,\n  `DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT` and `MCP_FLAKY_TAG`.\n* `tests/cli/eval/test_retry_policy.py` — regression suite locking the\n  contract in place.\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/design-spec.md §13` — Bounded retry\n  contract.\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/decisions.md §B` — OQ-10 deferral\n  record (target M3/M5).\n* `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/artifacts/D-0051/spec.md` — Per-task\n  deliverable record for T03.08.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":154,"oldLines":24,"newStart":154,"newLines":37,"lines":[" "," ## Operator-facing invariants"," ","-* `EvalRunner.DEFAULT_RETRY_COUNT` is the canonical pin. Goal\n\nLand the **opt-in retry-once branch** the design-spec §14 reserves\nfor MCP-flaky evals. Concretely:\n\n> *On the first non-PASS outcome whose status matches the flaky\n> taxonomy (FAIL, ERRORED, TIMEOUT) AND whose spec carries the\n> `MCP-flaky` capability tag, the runner re-executes the per-eval\n> lifecycle exactly once. The final outcome — whether the retry\n> recovered or the failure persisted — carries the\n> `mcp_server_flaky` artifact in `outcome.artifacts`.*\n\nFour deliverables in scope:\n\n1. New module `src/superclaude/cli/eval/retry.py` exporting\n   `RetryOncePolicy`, `MCP_FLAKY_TAG`, `MCP_SERVER_FLAKY_ARTIFACT`,\n   `is_mcp_flaky_tagged`, `is_flaky_outcome`.\n2. `EvalRunner` integration: additive `retry_policy` and\n   `home_factory` kwargs; `run()` consults the policy after each\n   first attempt and re-invokes the lifecycle via `_execute_once()`\n   when the policy elects retry.\n3. `docs/eval/retry.md` update reflecting the R3-mit contract: the\n   taxonomy table, manifest example, orthogonality with `retry_count`,\n   and OQ-10 closure note.\n4. `tests/cli/eval/test_mcp_retry_once.py` regression suite (26\n   tests) covering policy unit behaviour, EvalRunner integration, and\n   compatibility with the NFR-REL2 `retry_count` rejection.\n\nThe policy is **stateless and immutable** (frozen dataclass) — the\nrunner tracks attempt count externally so a stateful policy bug\ncannot loop.\n\n## 2. Public Surface\n\n```python\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.retry import (\n    MCP_FLAKY_TAG,                # \"MCP-flaky\" (mirrors EvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG)\n    MCP_SERVER_FLAKY_ARTIFACT,    # \"mcp_server_flaky\"\n    RetryOncePolicy,              # frozen dataclass; MAX_ATTEMPTS == 2\n    is_mcp_flaky_tagged,          # (EvalSpec) -> bool\n    is_flaky_outcome,             # (EvalOutcome) -> bool\n)\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.runner import EvalRunner\n\nEvalRunner(\n    ...,\n    retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy(),    # opt-in; default None disables R3-mit\n    home_factory=lambda: HomeIsolation(...),  # required in prod (setup is not re-entrant)\n)\n```\n\n### 2.1 RetryOncePolicy contract\n\n| Method | Returns | Contract |\n|---|---|---|\n| `is_eligible(spec)` | `bool` | `True` iff `MCP_FLAKY_TAG in spec.requires`. |\n| `should_retry(spec, outcome)` | `bool` | `True` iff `is_eligible(spec)` AND `is_flaky_outcome(outcome)`. The runner consults this only on the *first* attempt's outcome. |\n| `annotate(outcome)` | `EvalOutcome` | Returns a new outcome with `mcp_server_flaky=\"true\"` added to `outcome.artifacts`. Idempotent: re-application returns the input unchanged when the artifact is already present. |\n\n### 2.2 Flaky taxonomy\n\n| Status | Eligible | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| `FAIL` | Yes | MCP timeout expressed through expect callable |\n| `ERRORED` | Yes | Harness exception (often MCP transport) |\n| `TIMEOUT` | Yes | Most common MCP-flake signature |\n| `PASS` | No | Nothing to retry |\n| `SKIPPED` | No | Capability gate — did not run |\n| `INTERRUPTED` | No | SIGINT — operator intent |\n| `XFAIL` / `XPASS` | No | Expected-failure contract |\n\n### 2.3 EvalRunner integration\n\n`EvalRunner.run(spec)` now wraps `_execute_once(spec)` in a single\npolicy-gated retry branch:\n\n```python\noutcome = self._execute_once(spec)\nif self._retry_policy is not None and self._retry_policy.should_retry(spec, outcome):\n    if self._home_factory is not None:\n        self._home = self._home_factory()\n    retry_outcome = self._execute_once(spec)\n    outcome = self._retry_policy.annotate(retry_outcome)\nreturn outcome\n```\n\n`home_factory` is consulted only when wired. Production callers MUST\nwire one because `HomeIsolation.setup()` raises `RuntimeError` on a\nsecond call without an intervening teardown — the factory produces a\nfresh `HomeIsolation` so the second lifecycle sees the same contract.\nTest stubs whose `setup()` is callable across teardown may omit the\nfactory.\n\n## 3. Behavioural Contract\n\n### 3.1 Retry-once invariant\n\nFor every `EvalSpec` passed to `EvalRunner.run`:\n\n* If `retry_policy is None`: the executor trio fires **exactly once**\n  (NFR-REL2 default).\n* If `retry_policy` is wired AND `should_retry()` returns `False`:\n  the executor trio fires **exactly once**.\n* If `retry_policy` is wired AND `should_retry()` returns `True`:\n  the executor trio fires **exactly twice** — the original attempt\n  plus one retry. The policy never re-consults `should_retry()` on\n  the retry attempt's outcome.\n\n### 3.2 Artifact attachment\n\nThe `mcp_server_flaky` artifact is attached **after** the retry\nattempt completes, regardless of whether the retry's status is `PASS`,\n`FAIL`, `ERRORED`, or `TIMEOUT`. The artifact records *the fact\nthat a retry occurred*, not the result of the retry.\n\n| Scenario | First attempt | Retry attempt | Final status | Artifact present? |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Non-tagged eval, fails | FAIL | — | FAIL | No |\n| Tagged eval, passes | PASS | — | PASS | No |\n| Tagged eval, fails then passes | FAIL | PASS | PASS | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, fails persistently | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, errors then errors | ERRORED | ERRORED | ERRORED | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, times out then succeeds | TIMEOUT | PASS | PASS | Yes |\n\n### 3.3 Orthogonality with NFR-REL2\n\n| Construction | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| `retry_count=0`, `retry_policy=None` | NFR-REL2 default — no retry under any condition. |\n| `retry_count=0`, `retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy()` | R3-mit policy active for tagged evals only. |\n| `retry_count=1`, `retry_policy=None` | `ValueError` at construction time (NFR-REL2 guard). |\n| `retry_count=1`, `retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy()` | `ValueError` at construction time (NFR-REL2 guard not relaxed by policy presence). |\n\n## 4. Acceptance Criteria → Test Mapping\n\n| AC bullet | Test | Pin |\n|---|---|---|\n| Constants exist with canonical values | `test_constants_are_canonical` | `MCP_FLAKY_TAG == \"MCP-flaky\"`, `MCP_SERVER_FLAKY_ARTIFACT == \"mcp_server_flaky\"`, `EvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG == MCP_FLAKY_TAG` |\n| Tagged spec is eligible | `test_policy_is_eligible_for_tagged_spec`, `test_policy_is_eligible_for_tagged_spec_alongside_other_caps` | `RetryOncePolicy().is_eligible(spec) is True` |\n| Untagged spec is not eligible | `test_policy_not_eligible_for_untagged_spec`, `test_policy_not_eligible_when_only_other_caps_present` | `RetryOncePolicy().is_eligible(spec) is False` |\n| Flaky statuses trigger retry on tagged spec | Public Surface\n\n```python\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.retry import (\n    MCP_FLAKY_TAG,                # \"MCP-flaky\" (mirrors EvalRunner.MCP_FLAKY_TAG)\n    MCP_SERVER_FLAKY_ARTIFACT,    # \"mcp_server_flaky\"\n    RetryOncePolicy,              # frozen dataclass; MAX_ATTEMPTS == 2\n    is_mcp_flaky_tagged,          # (EvalSpec) -> bool\n    is_flaky_outcome,             # (EvalOutcome) -> bool\n)\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.runner import EvalRunner\n\nEvalRunner(\n    ...,\n    retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy(),    # opt-in; default None disables R3-mit\n    home_factory=lambda: HomeIsolation(...),  # required in prod (setup is not re-entrant)\n)\n```\n\n### 2.1 RetryOncePolicy contract\n\n| Method | Returns | Contract |\n|---|---|---|\n| `is_eligible(spec)` | `bool` | `True` iff `MCP_FLAKY_TAG in spec.requires`. |\n| `should_retry(spec, outcome)` | `bool` | `True` iff `is_eligible(spec)` AND `is_flaky_outcome(outcome)`. The runner consults this only on the *first* attempt's outcome. |\n| `annotate(outcome)` | `EvalOutcome` | Returns a new outcome with `mcp_server_flaky=\"true\"` added to `outcome.artifacts`. Production callers MUST\nwire one because `HomeIsolation.setup()` raises `RuntimeError` on a\nsecond call without an intervening teardown — the factory produces a\nfresh `HomeIsolation` so the second lifecycle sees the same contract.\nTest stubs whose `setup()` is callable across teardown may omit the\nfactory.\n\n## 3. Behavioural Contract\n\n### 3.1 Retry-once invariant\n\nFor every `EvalSpec` passed to `EvalRunner.run`:\n\n* If `retry_policy is None`: the executor trio fires **exactly once**\n  (NFR-REL2 default).\n* If `retry_policy` is wired AND `should_retry()` returns `False`:\n  the executor trio fires **exactly once**.\n* If `retry_policy` is wired AND `should_retry()` returns `True`:\n  the executor trio fires **exactly twice** — the original attempt\n  plus one retry. The policy never re-consults `should_retry()` on\n  the retry attempt's outcome.\n\n### 3.2 Artifact attachment\n\nThe `mcp_server_flaky` artifact is attached **after** the retry\nattempt completes, regardless of whether the retry's status is `PASS`,\n`FAIL`, `ERRORED`, or `TIMEOUT`. The artifact records *the fact\nthat a retry occurred*, not the result of the retry.\n\n| Scenario | First attempt | Retry attempt | Final status | Artifact present? |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Non-tagged eval, fails | FAIL | — | FAIL | No |\n| Tagged eval, passes | PASS | — | PASS | No |\n| Tagged eval, fails then passes | FAIL | PASS | PASS | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, fails persistently | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, errors then errors | ERRORED | ERRORED | ERRORED | Yes |\n| Tagged eval, times out then succeeds | TIMEOUT | PASS | PASS | Yes |\n\n### 3.3 Orthogonality with NFR-REL2\n\n| Construction | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| `retry_count=0`, `retry_policy=None` | NFR-REL2 default — no retry under any condition. |\n| `retry_count=0`, `retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy()` | R3-mit policy active for tagged evals only. |\n| `retry_count=1`, `retry_policy=None` | `ValueError` at construction time (NFR-REL2 guard). |\n| `retry_count=1`, `retry_policy=RetryOncePolicy()` | `ValueError` at construction time (NFR-REL2 guard not relaxed by policy presence). |\n\n## 4. The runner stores the policy on `self._retry_policy`; checking\n   `policy is not None` is a more readable conditional than\n   `should_retry_fn is not None`.\n3. The class collects the policy's three decision points\n   (`is_eligible`, `should_retry`, `annotate`) under one type so a\n   reader sees the contract at a glance instead of reconstructing it\n   from imports.\n\n### Why is the policy stateless?\n\nA stateful policy that tracked \"attempt count\" internally would have\nto be reset between evals; forgetting to reset is exactly the kind of\nbug the NFR-REL2 work was authored to prevent. The runner owns the\nattempt count externally (one consultation per `run()` call), so the\npolicy is stateless by construction.\n\n### Where does the `MCP-flaky` tag live?\n\nIn `EvalSpec.requires` — the existing field that accepts arbitrary\ncapability strings. Two reasons:\n\n1. The schema already accepts arbitrary strings there (one item per\n   capability gate) so no schema migration is required.\n2. Manifest authors already think of `requires:` as \"things this eval\n   depends on\" — flakiness is a property of the dependency set, not\n   the eval body.\n\nA future schema cleanup could promote it to a dedicated `tags:`\narray; the policy's `is_eligible()` would only need to swap the\nmembership check.\n\n### Why `home_factory` instead of re-initialising the existing home?\n\n`HomeIsolation.setup()` raises `RuntimeError` on a second call\nwithout intervening teardown — this is correct for the production\nclass because setup includes filesystem operations that would be\ndestructive to repeat. The runner therefore needs a way to obtain a\n*fresh* `HomeIsolation` for the retry attempt. Two options were\nconsidered:\n\n1. **Construct a new `HomeIsolation` in the runner.** Requires the\n   runner to know the home's construction parameters\n   (`eval_id`, `home_root`, ...). This couples the runner to the\n   isolation class's API.\n2. **Accept a `home_factory: Callable[[], HomeIsolation]` kwarg.**\n   The caller controls construction; the runner just invokes the\n   factory. Marking the\nattempts with a `retry_attempt: 0/1` field on each event would\nrequire schema changes to every event and a parser update on the\nReporter side. The `mcp_server_flaky` artifact key already records\n*that* a retry occurred; the JSONL log records *what happened* on\nthe second pass under the same event names as the first.\n\nIf a future operator need surfaces a per-attempt forensic\nrequirement, the additive change is small: add a `retry_attempt`\nfield to `_JsonlLog.emit()` and bump it after the policy elects\nretry.\n\n## Edge cases verified\n\n* **`MCP_FLAKY_TAG` alongside other capabilities.** The test\n  `test_policy_is_eligible_for_tagged_spec_alongside_other_caps`\n  pins eligibility when the tag sits beside real capability strings\n  like `mcp.tavily`. The tag is found by membership, not by being\n  the sole entry.\n* **Pre-existing artifacts survive annotation.** The test\n  `test_annotate_preserves_existing_artifacts` pins that\n  `mcp_server_flaky` is added to (not over) the existing artifact\n  map.\n* **Idempotency under re-annotation.** The test\n  `test_annotate_is_idempotent` pins that re-applying\n  `annotate(annotated)` returns the input unchanged.\n* **Recovery on retry still attaches the artifact.** The test\n  `test_retry_recovery_returns_pass_with_artifact` pins that a\n  PASS-after-FAIL run carries the artifact so the Reporter can\n  surface the flake-and-recover signal.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Trade-off | Choice | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| Retry vs. abort on policy programming error | Retry (current) | The policy is intentionally simple; the orchestrator already isolates eval failures. |\n| Annotate after recovery vs. only on persistent failure | Annotate both (current) | Reporter consumes a single signal; downstream tooling can compare against `status` to distinguish recovery from persistence. |\n| Wire policy on `EvalRunner` vs. on `RunOrchestrator` | `EvalRunner` (current) | The retry decision is per-eval, not per-suite; the runner already owns the per-eval lifecycle. |\n| Stateful vs. stateless policy | Stateless (current) | Avoids the \"forgot to reset between evals\" bug class entirely. |\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
